title: Air Defense Artillery Senior Sergeant
raw_text:
10-14Z. MOS 14Z--Air Defense Artillery Senior Sergeant, CMF 14
   a. Major duties. The ADA senior sergeant supervises, plans, coordinates, and directs the
emplacement, operation, unit level maintenance and management of air defense artillery weapon
systems in support of ADA units at all levels. Supervises and provides technical guidance to
subordinate Soldiers in the accomplishment of their duties. Supervises training, evaluations and
certification of AD crews in AD table training crew-drills. Monitors unit equipment readiness and
prepares monthly readiness reports. Performs inspections on maintenance records and demand
supported/diagnostics repair parts stockage procedures. Designs and implements the unit
maintenance programs. Coordinates with maintenance and logistical support activities. Performs
organizational planning, operations and training.
   b. Physical demands rating and qualifications for initial award of MOS. ADA senior sergeant
must possess the following qualifications:
        (1) A physical demands--N/A.
        (2) A physical profile of 222221.
        (3) Color discrimination of red/green.
        (4) A minimum score in aptitude area--N/A.
        (5) A security eligibility of SECRET is required for the initial award and to maintain the
MOS.
        (6) A U.S. citizen.
   c. Additional skill identifiers. (Note: Refer to table 12-8 (Listing of universal ASI’s associated
with all enlisted MOS)).
        (1) 4E – Air and Missile Defense Master Gunner (Effective 202710)
        (2) Q6--Protection Cell Operations (skill level 4 through 6 for personnel only)
         (3) R2—Stryker Leader (Personnel Only)
         (4) S5—M-SHORAD Master Gunner (Skill level 5 only).
         (5) T3—Ground-based Midcourse Defense (GMD) System.
         (6) T4—Patriot Master Gunner (Skill level 5 only).
   d. Physical requirements and standards of grade. Physical requirements and SG relating to
each skill level are listed in the following tables:
        (1) Table 10-14Z-1. Physical requirements.
        (2) Table 10-14Z-2. Standards of grade TOE/TMOE.
        (3) Table 10-14Z-3. Standards of grade TDA.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
